neighbours.label: ' ever' after 'be' in archaic moral exhortation ('let truth be ever thy guide')
fire: Let thy conscience be ever thy counsellor, and thy tongue be slow to anger.
May the Lord be ever merciful to the widow and the fatherless.
Let justice be ever the rule of thy dealings with thy neighbour.
Be ever watchful, my son, for the tempter walketh among men.
Let our hearts be ever turned toward the poor and the afflicted.
He bade his disciples to be ever humble and ever ready to forgive.
Let wisdom be ever thy companion and prudence thy guard.
O that my soul might be ever faithful to the vows I have made.
quiet: Let thy conscience be thy counsellor, and thy tongue be slow to anger.
May the Lord show mercy to the widow and the fatherless.
Let justice rule all thy dealings with thy neighbour.
Keep watch, my son, for the tempter walketh among men.
Let our hearts turn toward the poor and the afflicted.
He bade his disciples to be humble and ready to forgive.
Let wisdom go with thee and prudence guard thy steps.
O that my soul might keep faith with the vows I have made.

notes: Card: copula/adverb slot in 19th-century moral prose. Probe: 'be ever' 0.62-0.64; 'was greatly feared' 0.17; modern 'must be installed' ~0.
